metadata.description: Aaron's personal skills as plugins for Claude Code and Codex.

plugins.name: artifact-design
plugins.description: Claude Code's artifact-design, artifact-diagramming and dataviz skills for HTML artifacts, with Artifact and ArtifactCheck MCP tools that publish and preview them on this machine. From Anthropic's Claude Code.

plugins.name: create-skill
plugins.description: Write or revise an agent skill so it gives the model only the guidance it needs: start thin, write for the user's intent, and offer your own ideas as proposals the user picks from.

plugins.name: deeper-task
plugins.description: Ask for a deeper version of a task, not a bigger one: what an expert would do, the rawest material, their methods and tools, and an outside check, then a rewritten prompt. From Felix Rieseberg.

plugins.name: dj-fetch
plugins.description: Get DJ-ready tracks from a tracklist: Beatport decides the right version and length, free SoundCloud downloads cover bootlegs and edits, and slskd fetches the rest from Soulseek with paced searches and peer fallback.

plugins.name: eli5
plugins.description: Explain a topic to a complete beginner as an HTML artifact with big pictures and few words.

plugins.name: evals
plugins.description: Build an eval suite for a plugin, skill, instruction file or MCP server through an interview with sign-offs, save conversation moments as traces to build cases from, and hillclimb a target against its suite. Its own runner takes claude plugin eval's suites and runs them under Claude Code or Codex, with Opus judges, real instruction files, cases cut from real sessions and paired comparisons.

plugins.name: frontend-skill
plugins.description: Design visually strong landing pages, websites, apps, prototypes, and game UI with restrained composition and tasteful motion. From OpenAI.

plugins.name: implement-with-notes
plugins.description: Implement a spec while keeping a running implementation-notes.html of design decisions, deviations, tradeoffs, and open questions.

plugins.name: learn-how-i-write
plugins.description: Learn how you write from writing you point at (files, pasted text, docs, sent mail or messages) and save it as a reusable style profile, then restyle another piece, from a paper to an email, to sound like you without changing what it says. From Anthropic's Claude Duet.

plugins.name: mac-computer-use
plugins.description: Run Cua's cua-driver on Aaron's Mac mini from Grok Bot: an adapter that loads the driver's own skill on the Mac and covers only what differs when the Mac is another computer, plus a few facts about how this Mac is set up. Grok Bot only.

plugins.name: pakstack
plugins.description: Aaron's own working skills: interview (question the user until you both agree on what they want and why), catchup (pick up work left earlier) and the give-the-goal-not-the-how principle for writing prompts.

plugins.name: session-band
plugins.description: Clawd above the prompt with your session at a glance. Two looks: tide (the default) puts him on a little beach where the tide rises as context fills; hearth sets him beside three calm lines. Switch with /band or in /config. /band still keeps either look calm, and /band lively brings the motion back. In the terminal's fullscreen layout it steps aside while a / or @ menu is up, and the Band size row in /config keeps it to one row. Works in the terminal and the desktop Code tab. Claude Code only.

plugins.name: show-me
plugins.description: Explain the current topic visually with concise diagrams, code-shape sketches, and focused HTML artifacts. From HumanLayer.
